clue.text: Dispatch mission

definitions.meaning: dispatch here means speed and promptness in getting something done
a mission is a journey undertaken for a purpose, such as an exploring party

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses fit the one word: prompt haste ("with all expedition") and an organised journey with a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: promptness, a synonym of dispatch, and a purposeful journey, a synonym of mission.

clue.text: Discharge from river carrying power line

indicators.note: the river carries the power letter within it

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: Effluent released from a river that runs past a power line.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to drive out or eject, a synonym of discharge.

clue.text: Aristocrat, say, with monocle needs a wall mirror

indicators.note: say signals that the word for aristocrat is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility
a monocle is an eyeglass, a single glass

explanation.surface: A monocled lord needs a looking glass on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: A pier is the stretch of wall between windows, hence the name of the tall mirror hung there.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tall mirror hung on the wall space between two windows.

clue.text: Fitting introduction to a costume play

definitions.text: Fitting introduction to a costume play

parts.words: Fitting introduction to a costume play
parts.note: reads as a suitable preface to a period drama, but means the final full-costume run-through before opening night

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' looks like 'suitable', but hints at trying clothes on: this is the last rehearsal held in costume before the first night.
explanation.definitionFit: The last full rehearsal in costume comes just before, and so introduces, a play's run.

clue.text: Detailed claim by US state gets the bird

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed, with its last letter cut off

parts.note: a title is a right or claim, as to property
Ark. is the abbreviation for Arkansas

explanation.surface: An elaborate claim made by an American state is ridiculed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' means de-tailed: TITLE loses its last letter. 'gets the bird' on the surface means is booed.
explanation.definitionFit: The titlark is another name for the meadow pipit, a small bird.

clue.text: Source of lubricant old ailing diesel needed

indicators.note: ailing means unwell, out of order, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: An old, failing diesel engine needs a supply of lubricating oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ailing' looks like it describes the engine, but it is the anagram signal for the six letters of diesel; 'needed' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeds such as rape and linseed are pressed to yield oil, so they are a source of it.

clue.text: Fashionable man won't be seen in yellow

indicators.note: something that won't be seen in a word has been removed from it, signalling a deletion

parts.note: yellow is slang for cowardly, as is chicken
Ken is a man's name

explanation.surface: A stylish fellow refuses to be seen wearing yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't be seen in' takes KEN out of CHICKEN, leaving CHIC; 'yellow' is cowardly, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic is a direct synonym for stylish, meaning elegantly fashionable.

clue.text: Passes needed by crew

definitions.meaning: to pass something over to someone, as in passing the salt
the members of a ship's company, deckhands

explanation.walkthrough: One word as a verb means passes over; as a plural noun it means the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means passes something across; as a noun, the sailors of a ship.

clue.text: County second team has a handy opener

parts.note: Cork is a county in Ireland
a crew is a team, as of rowers

explanation.surface: A county's reserve side has a useful opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' suggests a cricket batsman, but the thing opens bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: The tool draws corks from wine bottles, so it is a handy bottle opener.

clue.text: Business that can't expect to succeed without a few hitches

definitions.text: Business that can't expect to succeed without a few hitches

parts.words: Business that can't expect to succeed without a few hitches
parts.note: hitches look like setbacks, but here mean weddings, getting hitched, which this agency needs to bring about

explanation.walkthrough: 'hitches' means snags on the surface, but getting hitched is getting married: a matchmaking agency succeeds only when clients wed.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchmaking agency introduces people with a view to marriage, so its success is weddings.

clue.text: Canon's order for payment of rate

definitions.meaning: a canon is a rule or principle of conduct
in British local government a ... is a demand from one authority to another for rate money

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is British local-government jargon: a precept is the order by which a body such as a county council claims its share of the local rates (property tax).
explanation.definitionFit: A rule of conduct is a synonym for canon, and a demand for rates is a technical sense in British administration.

clue.text: One not allowed to go for-a run unaccompanied

definitions.text: One not allowed to go for-a run unaccompanied

parts.words: One not allowed to go for-a run unaccompanied
parts.note: reads like a child or prisoner kept on a leash, but describes a novice British driver who must have a qualified person in the car

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a provisional licence holder may drive only with a qualified driver beside them, so they can never go for a run alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice driver on a provisional licence must be supervised, which is exactly the restriction described.

clue.text: Make rules for member I censure

parts.note: a leg is a limb, or member, of the body
to slate is to criticise harshly, British informal

explanation.surface: Someone drafting rules about a body part, then criticising it.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make laws, which is the same as making rules for something.

clue.text: Ramblers, for example, in the wars

definitions.meaning: rambler is a type of climbing rose, so ramblers are examples of the flower
the Wars of the ... were the fifteenth-century English civil wars between York and Lancaster

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ramblers' suggests hikers, but these are climbing flowers; 'in the wars' (hurt) hides a reference to the Wars of the Roses, England's 15th-century civil wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambling varieties are examples of the flower, and the dynastic wars took the flower's name.

clue.text: Stage holds exercises outside

indicators.note: the exercises word sits outside, wrapping the word for holds

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
has means holds or possesses

explanation.surface: A theatre stage hosting outdoor exercise sessions.
explanation.definitionFit: A phase is a stage in a process or development.

clue.text: Savoury dish a king wanted in thick fog

parts.note: pea soup is a savoury dish
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A traveller lost in fog wants a bowl of soup fit for a king.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is more often the Queen, but it is also the cipher of the Kings Edward (Edwardus Rex). A pea-souper is a thick yellow London fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea-souper is a dense yellowish fog, named for its likeness to the soup.

clue.text: Young nanny has head screwed on in Paris, for example

indicators.note: screwed on means attached after, so the head word follows

parts.note: a nanny goat's young is a kid
napper is British slang for the head

explanation.surface: A sensible nanny keeps a cool head on a trip to France.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris is not the French city but the Trojan prince who carried off Helen; NAPPER is old British slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Paris abducted Helen of Troy, so he is an example of an abductor.

clue.text: Going by bike from place to place selling, 'say

indicators.note: say signals that the selling word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: peddling is selling goods while travelling from place to place

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman cycles from town to town.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedalling means working a bicycle's pedals, so riding a bike.

clue.text: Smart dame fashionable in the Netherlands

indicators.note: fashionable here is read as fashioned, made into a new shape, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An elegant woman is stylish in Holland.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a place in the Netherlands, its capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch capital is a city in the Netherlands, so the phrase describes its location.

clue.text: Throw grenade to cause confusion

indicators.note: to throw something is to toss it about, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Lobbing a grenade to create chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into disorder or confusion.

clue.text: Diaphragm used in middle of jazz phrase

parts.note: mid means middle
a riff is a short repeated phrase in jazz or rock

explanation.surface: A musician breathes from the diaphragm in the middle of a jazz passage.
explanation.definitionFit: The midriff is the region over the diaphragm, and anatomically the diaphragm itself.

clue.text: Bequeath object to old wife

parts.note: an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: Leaving an item in a will to an elderly spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give property or income to someone, as a bequest does.

clue.text: Police officer recalled having to appear

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, the Northern Ireland police force
CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: A policeman summoned back to give evidence in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns the whole run RUCCO round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To occur is to happen or turn up, a synonym for appear.

clue.text: Enchantress (not English) article is about

indicators.note: not English means the letter standing for English is removed

parts.note: Circe is the enchantress in the Odyssey who turned men into pigs
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An essay on a sorceress, not an English one.
explanation.definitionFit: Circa, Latin for around, means about or approximately before a date.

clue.text: Increased disposition to be old and rude

indicators.note: disposition is read as arrangement, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Growing more inclined to be elderly and impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' means temperament on the surface but signals that BEOLD and RUDE are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Redoubled means intensified or increased, as effort is when doubled again.

clue.text: Duke stern and gloomy in poem

parts.note: the stern is the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: A severe duke appears gloomy in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' is not severe but a ship's back end. 'in poem' marks this as a poetic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, meaning dismal.

clue.text: Be part of Relate

definitions.meaning: to belong to something as a part or accessory
to have reference or connection to something

explanation.walkthrough: The italic Relate looks like the name of the British counselling charity, but is just the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to belong as a part and to have a bearing on something.

clue.text: List that's out of Times is incorrect

indicators.note: the that's letters stand out of, around, the rearranged word

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is

indicators.note: incorrect means wrongly arranged, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A list taken from The Times newspaper turns out to be wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is read as 'that is', abbreviated i.e.; 'incorrect' shuffles the newspaper name, and 'out of' puts the abbreviation round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to list things one by one.

clue.text: Erect tower

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to raise upright and to rise to a great height.

clue.text: One who complains about food recycled in fried mince

indicators.note: the complainer word goes about, around, the food word

parts.note: to beef is slang for to complain, so a beefer complains

indicators.note: recycled is read as cycled back, so the food word is read backwards

parts.note: grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: A grumbler protesting about reused food in a fry-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' is British slang for a complaint; 'recycled' turns the food slang backwards and 'about' wraps the complainer round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A burger is a patty of minced meat, usually fried or grilled.
